What Does "Separable" Mean?

A separable phrasal verb has two parts: a verb + a particle (up, on, off, out, away).

With a noun: two places are OK.
She put away the mugs. = She put the mugs away.

With a pronoun (it, them, him, her): the pronoun goes in the middle.
She put them away. ✓    She put away them. ✗
Watch out: never put a pronoun after the particle. Say verb + pronoun + particle.
 

The Seven Verbs

Phrasal verbMeaningExample
put awayreturn something to its proper placeShe put the mugs away.
hook upconnect the wires on a machine or applianceHe hooked the laptop up to the TV.
pick upstop to get someoneThe driver picked up the older man.
look uptry to find in a book or on the InternetShe looked up the price of a ticket.
pick outselect or choose somethingHe picked out a yellow shirt.
leave onnot turn off (an appliance or machine)He left the lamp on.
put offpostpone or delay somethingShe put off her haircut for two weeks.
 

Practice — Say It with a Pronoun

Change the CAPITALIZED words to it, them, him, or her. Say the new sentence, then click to check.

1. My cousin hooked up THE WASHING MACHINE.

My cousin hooked it up.

2. Dad left on THE HEADLIGHTS.

Dad left them on.

3. Grandma looked up THE PHONE NUMBER.

Grandma looked it up.

4. Carlos picked up HIS WIFE at the hospital.

Carlos picked her up at the hospital.

5. The school put off THE FIELD TRIP.

The school put it off.

6. I picked out TWO MELONS for the party.

I picked them out for the party.

7. Ben put away HIS JACKET.

Ben put it away.

 

Summary

Phrasal verbMeaningWith a pronoun
put awayreturn something to its proper placeput it / them away
hook upconnect the wires on a machine or appliancehook it / them up
pick upstop to get someonepick him / her up
look uptry to find in a book or on the Internetlook it / them up
pick outselect or choose somethingpick it / them out
leave onnot turn off (an appliance or machine)leave it / them on
put offpostpone or delay somethingput it / them off

Pronoun in the middle: verb + it + particle.
